preamble: The reduction of a voiceless postalveolar affricate /tʃ/ to a voiceless postalveolar fricative [ʃ] is an example of deaffrication. This process involves the loss of the initial stop component of the affricate, leaving only the fricative portion. In the Arawakan languages of Bolivia and Brazil, Terena turned the affricate *tʃ into ʃ, and Baure developed ʃ from *tʃ before front vowels.

examples.note: Word-initially Erzya has the affricate where Moksha has the fricative.
Terena changed its affricates to simple fricatives; Mojeño and Paunaka keep ʧ.
Baure /ʃ/ arose from *ʧ before i and e; the Muxojeóne variety keeps ʧ.
